title: Tab Smith, alto influence
summary: Tab Smith, whom he knew with Lucky Millinder, had a Hodges-like feel and later played with Basie alongside Earle Warren.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And we forgot about -- we forgot to mention another great saxophone player out of St. Louis, Tab Smith.
Oh, gee. He was another influence on a lot of alto players. I knew Tab when he first came with Lucky Millinder in the thirties. He was a great influence. He made a lot of good records.

Now, his sound, if you listen to him, he kind of came up like in Johnny Hodges' feel, I'll put it that way, feel of Johnny Hodges like that. He made a lot of good records and he had his own band for a long time but he got sick and died too

early, like a lot of the good musicians did. And he played with Basie too. He played with Basie in the forties. In fact Basie had him and Earle Warren there together. What more alto do you want than that, you know?
